presets.name: Top 10 large caps
presets.cardText: The 10 large caps with the strongest mix of business scores and price strength, from the FinLit score.
howItWorks: Only large caps: companies ranked 1 to 100 by market cap, as the site buckets them.
Market cap Rs 1,000 Cr or more.

Gates: Growth & Profitability score 65 or more, Technical 45 or more, Quality 50 or more, Balance sheet 45 or more (a blank is allowed for banks), no more than 30% below the 52-week high, and a 1-year return of 300% or less.

Ranked by a weighted score: each input is the company's percentile among the companies of its size group with a market cap of Rs 1,000 Cr or more: Growth & Profitability 50%, Technical 20%, momentum 15% (the momentum score of the Momentum leaders card), 52-week position 10% (100 minus the % below the high) and Quality 5%.
At most 3 companies from one Sector label. Ties go to the higher Growth & Profitability score, then the higher FinLit IQ.
A company with a blank score drops out of any rule that uses that score.
presets.disclaimer: A screen narrows a list. It is not a recommendation.

presets.name: Sector themes in play
presets.cardText: Sectors where more stocks sit near their 52-week high than in the market as a whole, and the companies leading them.

chips.label: Include small groups
chips.description: Also lists industries with 5 to 7 companies, which are too few to call a theme with the same confidence.

howItWorks: Every night each sector (by its Sector label) is scored on breadth, the share of its stocks within 15% of their 52-week high, and its median 3-month return against the whole market; stocks of Rs 1,000 Cr or more.
In play: breadth at least 40% and 15 points above the market's, and median 3-month return at least 5 points above the market's.
Leaders (up to 5 per sector): market cap Rs 1,000 Cr or more, within 15% of their 52-week high, 3-month return above the sector median; ranked by the Top 10 rank score of the Basic tab.
Generic labels (Capital Goods, Financial Services, Services, FMCG, Healthcare, Information Technology) and groups under 8 companies are left out of theme status.
